definitions.definition: How well information stays the same and makes sense when it is copied or passed along.
definitions.example: A game of telephone where the message stays almost exactly the same after many people whisper it.

definitions.definition: A measure of how much a text's original meaning survives being copied, translated, and spread over time.
definitions.example: Checking if a recipe still tastes the same after being passed down through five generations.

definitions.definition: The study of how information is stored, sent, and how much gets lost or corrupted.
definitions.example: Figuring out how many typos you can expect when copying a book by hand.

definitions.definition: A rule that says erasing or losing information always creates a tiny amount of heat and disorder.
definitions.example: Every time you delete a file on a computer, a tiny bit of energy is released as heat.

definitions.definition: The law that says things naturally become more messy and disordered over time unless energy is used to keep them organized.
definitions.example: Your bedroom gets messier on its own; you have to work to clean it up.

definitions.definition: A measure of disorder or randomness in a system; in information, it means how much uncertainty or noise there is.
definitions.example: A shuffled deck of cards has high entropy; a deck in order by suit has low entropy.

definitions.definition: Unwanted changes or errors that mess up a signal or message.
definitions.example: Static on a radio that makes the song hard to hear.

definitions.definition: The actual useful information being sent, without the errors or noise.
definitions.example: The words your friend says on a crackly phone line, not the crackling sound.

definitions.definition: A handwritten copy of a document, especially from before printing presses existed.
definitions.example: A monk's handwritten copy of a book from the Middle Ages.

definitions.definition: The percentage of words or sentences that are exactly the same when comparing different copies of the same text.
definitions.example: If two students copy the same sentence and 99 out of 100 words match, that's 99% textual agreement.

definitions.definition: Made up of several different parts combined together.
definitions.example: A smoothie is a composite of fruits, yogurt, and juice.

definitions.definition: Things that put pressure on a text and make it harder for it to stay the same over time.
definitions.example: Age, translation, and copying mistakes are all stress factors for an old document.

definitions.definition: The process of something getting worse, weaker, or less accurate over time.
definitions.example: An old photograph fading and becoming blurry.

definitions.definition: A jumbled mess of information that has no clear meaning or pattern.
definitions.example: The sound of a radio tuned between stations, just static and hissing.
